plain: This story is about Francis Crick, the scientist who helped discover the double helix shape of DNA. According to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, Crick wrote a paper in 1973 on "directed panspermia," the idea that life on Earth was deliberately seeded from space by another intelligence. A writer on ancient history, Graham Hancock, describes the idea vividly: a spaceship carrying bacteria hit the early Earth and spilled out its contents. Hancock points to Crick's later book, Life Itself. Michels returns to it on several episodes, once mentioning a second date, 1981, and noting that Crick was a former associate of his guest, the scientist Rupert Sheldrake. In another episode he simply says Crick proposed the idea, with no date or paper. Michels and Hancock tell it in their own words. If the idea were right, life on Earth would have been planted on purpose by someone else.
